method: Direct visual inspection of all sixteen PNG checkpoints decoded from the final H.264 movie; complete frame decoding and native source/import checks are recorded separately. This is sampled movie review, not a claim that all 859 movie frames were visually inspected. Every authored integer animation pose is covered by the independent four-view atlas review reports.
checkpoint_image_source: Decoded from the final movie at the listed zero-based native_movie_frame values; PNGs retained in inspect/r4_demo_movie_frames.
camera_repair: The initial movie review found the platform hiding the jump feet/obstacle. Only the capture harness jump camera was adjusted to yaw -0.60, distance 3.20 m and pitch 0.14 before a complete native re-record. All sixteen final movie checkpoints were then viewed again; no product/fixture/physics retiming or changes occurred.

checkpoints.notes: Actual F1 startup is visible with Zombie.glb, four clips, the Original/Main selection and the Run R4 demonstration button. Whole subject and controls are readable.

Actual Run button has selected R4, the loaded label shows Zombie.r4.glb and 15 clips, and live pursuit begins. Whole walking subject is visible; the far target partly lies under the left HUD at the start of pursuit.

Bite contact is indicated by the orange pad and first contact/86 HP. The head, bent arms and whole stance are visible; the target partly hides the mouth from this three-quarter view, with detailed surface contact covered by the separate four-angle outcome review.
Left-arm strike reaches the exposed rectangular pad, with the other arm bent separately. Orange contact feedback, left-attack label, two contacts and 76 HP agree.
Right-arm strike uses the opposite arm and distinct torso/stance; right-attack label, orange contact feedback, three contacts and 64 HP agree.
The double-hand strike presents both arms forward and a braced lower body, with both-attack label, four contacts and 46 HP. Shirt and elbow silhouettes are coherent.

The corrected open jump angle now shows the complete body, both boots and the yellow 10 cm obstacle. The platform and ladder no longer hide the feet; compact bent knees and raised arms read as a small hop.
Ladder traversal shows both arms, the offset hand reaches, both boots and the rungs. The target remains behind the ladder without hiding the main body; the climb action label matches.
After one-leg loss the live subject is prone; the detached leg is moving physically in the foreground and the retained leg remains attached. The status names the severed left thigh.
One-leg crawl pursuit shows alternating arm support, the intact leg, detached leg and low target. The target has moved relative to the subject, and the live crawl label matches.
One-leg crawl bite reaches the lowered sphere, with five contacts and 36 rounded HP. The mouth remains outside the bulk of the target while the hands brace the body.
After the second leg loss, the body continues crawling with two detached leg chains behind. Low target, arm positions, missing-leg count and crawl stage are readable.
The second prone bite shows visible orange target contact feedback, six contacts and 26 rounded HP. The body and both detached leg chains remain visible.
The completed-cycle state displays Crawl Idle and the four-second restore countdown, preserving six contacts and the final target health.
Actual Stop button has ended the demo, hidden the target and restored the Run button with orbit/frame inspection available. The existing prone subject and detached legs remain in the scene.
The final decoded frame remains a valid stopped inspection view with the Run button available and a continuing prone idle pose; no blank or truncated final frame.

findings: All action/stage HUD labels match the sampled live poses.
Four standing attack variants, actual hop, ladder and one-/both-leg crawling are visible in the final recording.
Six actual validated contacts occur during a completed cycle; actual Run and Stop button events are recorded.
The final jump view resolves both feet and the obstacle; detailed contact and limb inspection is supplemented by all 44 native multi-angle outcome stills.
